messages:
Elliot Price: Need final wording lock today for the marketplace docs/FAQ security section (AWS + GCP pages). @Marcus Lin can you sanity check the current copy below? Goal is “accurate, review-safe, doesn’t overpromise.”

Elliot Price: Current draft in docs PR:

> Security & Compliance
> - Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report and follows ISO 27001-aligned controls.
> - Data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
> - Audit logs are available for administrative actions and API access.
> - Customer data is not used to train models.
> - Data residency: you can choose the region where your data is processed.

Elliot Price: Flags: “ISO 27001-aligned” and the “audit logs” line might be too broad? Please suggest exact replacement text if needed.

Kira Thompson: Adding the longer FAQ answer block too (this is what customers will copy/paste into procurement questionnaires):

Kira Thompson: 
Q: Do you have SOC 2 / ISO 27001?
A: Redwood Inference is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.

Q: Is data encrypted?
A: Yes, we encrypt customer data at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).

Q: Do you provide audit logs?
A: Yes. Audit logs are available for all activity and can be exported.

Q: Do you train on customer data?
A: No. Redwood does not train on customer prompts or completions.

Q: Can I control retention / deletion?
A: Yes, Redwood supports configurable retention and deletion on request.

Marcus Lin: Yep, a few things to tighten. Main issue: we shouldn’t say “ISO 27001 certified” anywhere. We’re not certified. We can say “security program is aligned with common standards (e.g., ISO 27001)” but even that can get interpreted as “equivalent.” Better to keep it factual: SOC 2 Type II + internal control framework.

Marcus Lin: Also “SOC 2 Type II compliant” is not how auditors like it phrased. Use “SOC 2 Type II report available” / “has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit” (and note: report under NDA).

Marcus Lin: Audit logs: “available for all activity” is too broad. We have audit logging for *administrative actions* in the Console and certain API events; coverage varies by product surface and deployment mode. Also “can be exported” is true in Dedicated/Private with log forwarding; Hosted has limited export options depending on plan.

Marcus Lin: Retention: “configurable retention” is only for certain tiers / add-ons (retention controls + log retention). We can say “options available” and point to Sales for exact config.

Marcus Lin: Proposed replacement copy (docs-safe):

Marcus Lin:
- SOC 2: “Redwood Inference has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. The SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA upon request.”
- ISO: remove “certified”. If you need a line: “Redwood maintains a security program based on industry-standard control frameworks.” (no ISO callout)
- Encryption: keep, but avoid guaranteeing algorithms everywhere. “TLS” + “encryption at rest” is enough.
- Audit logs: “Redwood provides audit logs for administrative actions in the Redwood Console. Log availability and export options vary by deployment (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).”
- Training: “By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts or completions to train or fine-tune models.” (add “by default”)
- Residency: careful: we process in the region selected *for the deployment*, but control plane + support access can complicate. Suggest: “Customers can select the region for their deployment. Data processing occurs in the selected region for supported products.”

Naomi Feldman: +1 on all of Marcus’ flags. We’ve had marketplace reviewers push back when they see “ISO 27001” anywhere unless it’s a hard cert.

Olga Petrov: Adding GRC nuance: we can also say “SOC 2 Type II report covering the Redwood Inference platform” but avoid listing Trust Services Criteria unless we’re exact. And please add “available under NDA” explicitly.

Olga Petrov: Re: retention wording: if we say “deletion on request,” that’s OK but we should avoid implying we can delete data that the customer controls in Private/on-prem (that’s on them). Maybe phrase as: “Redwood supports data deletion requests for applicable hosted services; in Private deployments, customers control data lifecycle.”

Kira Thompson: Got it. I can remove ISO references entirely. For encryption, do we want to keep TLS 1.2+ / AES-256 or make it generic?

Marcus Lin: I’d make it generic in the public docs, and keep specifics for the security packet. For marketplace docs/FAQ, stick with:
- “Encrypted in transit using industry-standard TLS”
- “Encrypted at rest using industry-standard encryption mechanisms”

Marcus Lin: (The moment we put AES/TLS versions in docs, it’s now a commitment / needs maintenance.)

Elliot Price: Makes sense. Can we land final “copy/paste” blocks here so I can update PR-4821 and the marketplace FAQ page?

Marcus Lin: Here’s suggested final text (use as-is):

Marcus Lin:
**Security & Compliance (Marketplace FAQ)**
- **SOC 2:** Redwood Inference has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. The SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA upon request.
- **Encryption:** Customer data is encrypted in transit and at rest using industry-standard mechanisms.
- **Audit logs:** Redwood provides audit logs for administrative actions in the Redwood Console. Audit log availability and export options vary by deployment (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and plan.
- **Use of customer data for training:** By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts or completions to train or fine-tune models.
- **Data residency:** Customers can select the region for their deployment. Data processing occurs in the selected region for supported products.
- **Retention & deletion:** Retention options are available by plan. Redwood supports deletion requests for applicable hosted services; in Private deployments, customers control data lifecycle.

Olga Petrov: Please add one more sentence to SOC2 line: “Redwood can share a bridge letter upon request when applicable.” (Some enterprise buyers ask during renewal window.) If that’s too much for docs, keep it in the security packet only.

Marcus Lin: I’d keep bridge letter out of docs. It’s not always available and creates follow-up. Security packet / GRC request process handles it.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. Keep marketplace docs minimal + factual. The block Marcus posted looks good. Only tweak I’d make: on residency, avoid “occurs” (absolute). Maybe “is designed to occur” / “is configured to occur” in the selected region.

Marcus Lin: Good call. Revised residency line:
- **Data residency:** Customers can select the region for their deployment. For supported products, data processing is configured to occur in the selected region.

Kira Thompson: Perfect. I’ll update the FAQ answers accordingly and remove ISO mentions. Also adjusting training answer to “By default…”

Elliot Price: Thank you all. I’m updating the docs PR now with the exact block + the revised residency sentence. @Marcus Lin @Dr. Aisha Rahman can you react :thumbsup: here once you’ve scanned the final diff?

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup:

Dr. Aisha Rahman: :thumbsup:

Olga Petrov: :thumbsup: (and thanks for pulling ISO out)

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: once merged, I’ll link this wording from the security packet so we stay consistent.
